title: Monitor, collect and collate agricultural data

lessons.title: What data to collect
lessons.html:
Why farms collect data

Data means facts and numbers. Farms collect data to know what is happening and to make good decisions. For example: How much rain fell? How many calves were born? How many crates were picked?

Examples of farm data

AreaData
WeatherRainfall in mm, temperature, frost
CropsCrates or tons picked per land, plant counts, pest counts
AnimalsBirths, deaths, weights, treatments, number in each camp
WaterMeter readings, dam levels
InputsBags of feed used, litres of diesel
WorkHours worked, tasks done

Know what is needed

Before you start, ask your supervisor:

  • What data must I collect?
  • Where and when?
  • Which tool or form do I use?
  • Who gets the data?

Collecting data well

  • Use the right tool: rain gauge, scale, measuring tape, counter, meter or tablet.
  • Make sure the tool is clean and working. A scale must show zero before you weigh.
  • Collect at the same time and in the same way each time. For example, read the rain gauge every morning at 08:00.
  • Write the data down straight away. Do not trust your memory.
  • Write clearly. Use numbers and units, such as 12 mm or 245 kg.
  • If you make a mistake, draw one line through it and write the right number next to it. Do not scratch it out.

Check that your tool works before you go out.

Keep the forms clean and dry. A wet, dirty form is hard to read. Put it in a plastic sleeve or a clipboard with a cover.

lessons.title: Collating data and making a report
lessons.html:
Putting data together

To collate means to bring data together and put it in order. Then it is easy to read and use.

Steps

  1. Collect all the forms or pages for the period, for example one week.
  2. Check each one: is the date there? Are numbers missing? Do any look wrong?
  3. Sort them, for example by date, by land or by camp.
  4. Add up totals and work out averages.
  5. Write them in the table or form the farm uses, or type them into the computer.

Example: weekly picking report

DayLand 1 cratesLand 2 crates
Monday12080
Tuesday13090
Wednesday11070
Total360240

The average for Land 1 is 360 divided by 3 days, which is 120 crates a day.

Writing the report

  • Use the format your supervisor asks for.
  • Put a heading: what the report is about, the dates, and your name.
  • Show the numbers in a table.
  • Write one or two short sentences about anything unusual. For example: "Land 2 picking was low on Wednesday because of rain."
  • Hand it in on time to the right person. Keep a copy.

Farm data is private. Do not share it with people outside the farm without permission.

If a number looks very strange, check it again before you put it in the report. For example, 1 200 crates in a day when normal is 120 may be a mistake.

Ask your supervisor if you do not understand the report format. It is better to ask than to make a mistake.

lessons.title: Staying safe while collecting data
lessons.html:
Health and safety

Collecting data takes you all over the farm: into lands, kraals, dams and stores. Each place has dangers. Think before you go.

In the lands

  • Do not enter a land that was just sprayed. Check the re-entry time with your supervisor.
  • Wear a hat, long sleeves and sunscreen. Drink enough water.
  • Watch for snakes. Wear boots. Do not put your hand where you cannot see.
  • Keep away from working tractors and harvesters.

With animals

  • Never go into a pen with a bull alone.
  • Stay calm and quiet. Do not stand behind horses or cattle.
  • Use the crush when you must weigh or check animals.
  • Wash your hands after touching animals.

At dams, tanks and stores

  • Do not lean over dam walls or climb into tanks to read levels.
  • Do not go into a grain silo or a store that has been fumigated.
  • Read chemical store data only with permission and with the door open for air.

With equipment

  • Carry tablets and phones carefully. Keep them dry and charged.
  • Lift scales and heavy equipment with bent knees and a straight back, or ask for help.
  • Do not work in a lightning storm. Go inside.

If there is an accident, tell your supervisor at once. Report anything unsafe that you see.

Key points

  • Know what data is needed, where, when and with which tool.
  • Write data down straight away with numbers and units.
  • Collate by checking, sorting, adding totals and averages.
  • Report in the required format and hand it in on time.
  • Stay safe: sprayed lands, animals, dams and storms are dangers.
